idiom_name: libxml2 logical page + libxslt stylesheet per channel (xsltApplyStylesheet)
implementation_notes: Stage one builds the logical page as a libxml2 document - xmlNewDoc, xmlNewNode, xmlNewChild, xmlNewProp - with domain element names and no HTML decoration; xmlSaveFormatFile or xmlDocDumpMemory snapshots it for tests or caching. Stage two hands that document to xsltParseStylesheetFile and xsltApplyStylesheet with one stylesheet per channel, then writes the result with xsltSaveResultToFile or xsltSaveResultToString, so HTML, plain text and XSL-FO/PDF all come from the same page. libxml2 plus libxslt is the standard XSLT vehicle for C, which makes this a library realization rather than a hand-built renderer; hand-rolled printf emitters are Transform View, not this pattern, because no logical page survives between the two stages.
pitfalls: libxml2 and libxslt ownership is manual: every xmlDocPtr and xsltStylesheetPtr must be freed (xmlFreeDoc, xsltFreeStylesheet), or a long-running renderer leaks a whole page per request.

libxslt has no sandbox for stylesheets. Entity substitution and external subset loading are driven by global parser flags (xmlSubstituteEntitiesDefault, xmlLoadExtDtdDefaultValue), so never load a stylesheet you did not author.
The factory and its stylesheet are process-global state: libxslt extension modules registered for one channel are visible to every other renderer in the process.
